TextBlock.Text: Classify both reconnaissance contacts as hostile, then withdraw both fighters. Fictional 2025 operation; requires F-23A Block 40 and Block 40 Strike.

Two scouts are observing the shipping lane. WIDOW 11 and 12 start 30 nautical miles west of the first reported contact. Enemy fighters patrol farther east. A civilian airliner is crossing north of the area.

Radar starts OFF and infrared search ON. Classify each scout as hostile; the task requires both contacts, and does not require exact type identification. Preserve both scouts until confirmation. Radar use is permitted if passive search is insufficient.

After headquarters confirms both contacts, bring BOTH F-23s into the western withdrawal circle at 26,000 feet. The circle activates only after the reconnaissance task. Losing either F-23 or a scout before confirmation fails. Keeping both fighters unclassified by the enemy earns a bonus.

Your aircraft start airborne and selected, with weapons and fuel loaded. Two-aircraft flights begin in Vic formation. Give route and attack orders to the flight leader, or detach a wingman for independent tasking.

Fictional naval F-23 development in September 2025. The carrier, supporting units and legacy opposition are scenario stand-ins. Radar silence does not guarantee invisibility. Neutral losses anywhere in the scenario fail the operation.
